jobs.title: Staff Product Manager - Trips
jobs.description:
Hi! 👋 I'm Steven, Lead Product Manager at WeTravel

I'm hiring a Staff PM to own Trips, the domain where every trip comes to life. Ten thousand travel businesses build, present, and sell their trips with WeTravel, from boutique agencies to student travel operators running hundreds of departures a year, which makes this both the surface their teams spend most of their working day in and the first thing their travelers ever see. You'll own it end to end: the trip page they sell with, and the content and AI engine that crafts it, and the content specialists who build our library, who will report to you.

About WeTravel

Travel gives people new experiences and brings them together, sometimes in life-changing ways. That's especially the case for group travel and multi-day travel (think of a 7-day safari in the Serengeti, a 5-day scuba diving trip in the Galápagos, or a multi-week pilgrimage) where travelers get to really immerse themselves. Passionate travel organizers make this magic happen, and WeTravel is here to support them.

Multi-day travel businesses use WeTravel as their end-to-end operating system: publishing trip offerings, generating and converting leads, processing payments around the world, paying suppliers and vendors. WeTravel helps them grow sales, save time, and save money, so they can focus on delivering incredible bucket-list experiences.

WeTravel is a 400+ person company representing more than 50 countries. We combine global diversity with the agility and closeness of a much smaller team. More than 90 colleagues are based in our Amsterdam office in Rokin, including the entire Product Org and most of our Engineering team.

You will have fun innovating fast with brilliant, low-ego colleagues. Our clients are also easy to reach, which helps us stay close to their needs and build with them.

Financially, WeTravel is highly secure and growing fast, with 50 to 100 percent year-over-year growth depending on the metric. This gives us a strong foundation to build from.

About the Role

This is the domain where our biggest bet is playing out. Building and selling a great multi-day trip is a lot of work: crafting a story worth booking, assembling the content that tells it, and presenting it all in a page a traveler trusts. Our goal is to cut that turnaround down so organizers get back to their client faster, convert more of them, and sell more trips. It also has to hold up as they grow, because a boutique agency selling bespoke trips and a student travel operator running hundreds of departures are building on the same tools. The way we get there is great technology in the hands of organizers and their teams. You will own that end to end, the experience and the engine behind it.

What you'll work on

WeTravel Trips give organizers the tools to create proposals, detailed itineraries and a high-conversion booking experience, while giving them time back to grow and operate their business.

We're now looking for a Staff PM to take this domain through its next phase of growth, and make WeTravel the best software for travel businesses to build, present and sell their trips.

Our success in this domain will drive the growth of our organizers by expanding in several areas:

  • An integrated building experience that helps organizers find the right content and craft the right trip for the right travelers.

  • Shared libraries that pay off most when a team works from them, so every proposal that leaves the company is consistent, beautiful, and unmistakably theirs, whoever wrote it.

  • AI-enabled tools to imagine and create new trips, produce world class content, and optimize their sales funnel.

  • Trip pages organizers can publish and promote wherever their travelers are.

1/ Designing the trip page and selling the trip

Think of the trip page as the product detail page of the travel industry. It is where an organizer's work becomes something a traveler wants, understands, and buys.

  • Dynamic Trip Builder: Intuitive tools for organizers to create their trip offerings, in the languages their travelers read, on WeTravel and beyond it.

  • Day by day itineraries: the plan that makes a trip feel real before anyone has booked it, built fast and kept accurate as the trip changes.

  • High converting pages and proposals: whether an organizer publishes a trip for the world or sends a tailored proposal to one client, the result has to look professional, capture travelers' imaginations, and turn interest into a booking.

  • Mobile app for travelers: once they have booked, travelers carry the trip page in their pocket, with everything they need before and during it.

2/ The content and AI engine that turns hours of work into minutes

  • WeTravel Library: a curated library of properties, activities, and reusable content on its way to 20,000 properties, so organizers build with high quality content.

  • The organizer's own library: their photos, their descriptions, their reusable blocks, so a growing team sells in one voice instead of rewriting content from scratch.

  • AI-assisted building: Copilot that drafts and improves trips inside the builder, so organizers start from a strong draft rather than an empty page.

And the team behind it. Our content specialists will report to you, and you will own the content strategy, the regional prioritization, and the pipeline that keeps the library growing.

I'm looking for an experienced, generalist product manager to lead this domain end-to-end. You will deeply study travel organizers' needs, prioritize them, come up with solutions (or hypotheses to test), drive all necessary functions to build and launch the solutions, drive adoption, and ultimately grow our revenue and profit. You will also manage our content team, and you will have direct and continuous access to C-level executives to ideate and create products.

If you've ever wanted to empower businesses with innovative tech and have fun in a well-funded rocketship in the heart of Amsterdam, this is it.

An Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate would bring a track record of exceptional results and a well-rounded product management skill set, especially the ability to break down any problem and drive high-velocity execution.

Must-haves:

  • Deep product management experience owning real outcomes, not just execution.

    • 10+ years in product management is ideal (for staff level)

    • 7+ years is minimum (for senior level)

  • Travel industry knowledge.

  • Comfortable being accountable for product-led commercial outcomes, not just features shipped.

  • Strong cross-functional stakeholder leadership across sales / account management, engineering, design.

  • Growth and experimentation mindset, with the judgment to decide without perfect data. Willing to ship, learn, and iterate.

  • Data self-sufficient. You can pull your own numbers, find where a funnel leaks, and size the opportunity before asking for engineering time.

Things that will likely help you in this particular role:

  • You have owned a builder, editor or CMS-like product where the artifact your users create is what earns them money.

  • You have shipped AI features that people kept using, and you can tell the difference between a good demo and real adoption.

  • You have treated content as product, not as someone else's job, and have worked with or led a content operation.

  • Experience with public APIs, webhooks, or platform work.

  • Experience managing people, even a small team or a dotted line.

Interview process

Our process aims to be high-signal and help you learn about WeTravel and our people. Two interviews will be realistic working sessions. No take-home assignments. The whole process will take only a few weeks.

Screen

  • Recruiter screen (30 min): introduction, background, motivation.

1st round

2nd round

jobs.title: Staff Frontend Engineer / Frontend Architect (m/f/d)
jobs.description:
Introduction

Teaser

Two products, two backends, one frontend vision: build the AI-first frontend platform and design system that lets our engineers, product managers and designers ship UI at speed. A senior hands-on role with architect-level influence, no people management, and our CPTO as your executive sponsor.

Role at a glance

  • Level: Staff/Principal-level individual contributor – technical leadership, no direct reports
  • Reporting line: VP Engineering. Executive sponsor: our CPTO
  • Products: FactFinder NG (React on a Java backend) and Infinity (React on a .NET/F# backend)
  • Stack you'll shape: React, TypeScript, Web Components, design tokens, Storybook, AI coding tools (Claude Code, Cursor, MCP-based tooling)
  • Team: Product & Technology organization of around 25 people, led by our CPTO, working in a product trio model with product and design
  • Location: Berlin; Munich, Pforzheim or Stockholm possible – hybrid with 2–3 office days per week; occasional travel (<10%) for offsites and design-system workshops
  • Start: as soon as possible

About FactFinder

FactFinder is one of the leading product discovery platforms for European eCommerce. For more than 20 years we've applied AI and machine learning to product search, navigation, personalization and recommendations. Our Product Discovery Experience (PDX) spans two products: FactFinder NG, an exact and highly configurable search, and Infinity, a self-learning, behavioral discovery engine. More than 2,000 customers generate over €160 billion in annual GMV on our platform.

We're around 90 people with a new management team, a clear growth plan and reknown investors behind us. Right now we're rebuilding our product and tech organization around an AI-first way of working and agentic commerce – and this role sits at the center of it.

Why this role exists

Our two products run two React frontends with very different technical roots. We need a vision, an architect, and an owner — someone who will unify them into a single, efficient system, build the shared design system on top, and enable product managers and designers to prototype and ship production-grade UI themselves with AI tooling. Incrementally, without a big-bang rewrite, and while both products keep shipping.


Your mission

What you'll do

  • Define and drive the target frontend architecture across both React products – one consistent, efficient React-based system, migrated step by step
  • Build and own our shared design system: tokens, component library and Web Components for embeddable shop UI, tightly aligned with Product Design
  • Create an AI-first prototyping and contribution framework – design system, AI coding tools, guardrails, automated review and CI – so product managers and designers can prototype and contribute production-grade UI
  • Stay hands-on: write a significant share of the critical code, set standards, and pair with and level up our frontend engineers
  • Work with a clear operating split: after architecture-focused first stints, spend around 80% of your time hands-on coding and 20% on architecture, design-system leadership and enablement
What success looks like
  • After 90 days: frontend audit of both products done, target architecture and migration roadmap agreed, design-system tokens and core components live, and the first prototype built and shipped by a product manager or designer on the new framework
  • After 12 months: both products run on the shared design system, the frontend rework shows measurable efficiency gains, and product and design prototype independently as a routine – frontend is no longer the bottleneck


Your profile

Must-have

  • Expert-level React and TypeScript, proven in complex production SaaS frontends
  • A real AI-first engineering practice: you use AI coding tools and agents daily and have built workflows or frameworks that others use – not just "I use Copilot"
  • Design-system architecture: you've built or led a design system (tokens, component library, Storybook or similar) that was adopted across multiple teams or products
  • Web Components (Custom Elements, Shadow DOM, embedding in third-party environments) plus a frontend architecture track record: you've modernized or migrated a frontend stack at least once, ideally several times
  • 6+ years in frontend or software engineering, including 3+ years at Staff, Lead or Architect level – setting technical direction across teams, not just within your own
  • Hands-on today: you write production code yourself – this is not a concept-only architect position
  • Business-fluent English (C1); no formal degree required, your track record counts
Nice-to-have
  • Technical leadership without line management: you've led a SaaS frontend team through a major technology change
  • Meta-frameworks such as Next.js and/or Astro – and a clear view on when to use which
  • Design-to-code and prototyping tooling: Figma workflows, design-token pipelines, AI UI generation (v0, Claude Code, Cursor, MCP-based tooling)
  • eCommerce, search or product discovery frontends (search UIs, embeddable shop widgets)
  • React on non-JavaScript backends (Java/Spring, .NET); Fable/Feliz or Ant Design
  • Good German language skills


Bonus Points

Who thrives here

  • Builders who ship code themselves and lead by example
  • Pragmatic simplifiers: incremental migration over big-bang rewrites, no over-engineering
  • Change agents with strong opinions, weakly held – able to transform an organization without burning it out
  • Enablers who enjoy making product managers and designers productive and treat them as peers
Probably not for you if you'd rather produce architecture concepts than running code, want to go deep on one product and leave the cross-product system to others, or are looking for a people-management role.


THE JOY OF WORKING WITH US

What we offer

  • Real ownership with executive backing: you shape the frontend of two products end to end. You report to our VP Engineering; our CPTO is the executive sponsor of this role – both agree the target architecture and migration roadmap with you, and the CPTO reviews your 90-day goals and holds your final interview. A company-level priority, not a side project
  • AI-first as a leadership priority, with the tooling budget to match: Claude Code, Cursor or whatever makes you fastest
  • Impact without switching to management: a Staff/Principal IC track on our career ladder toward Principal/Distinguished – with the option to move into engineering management later if you want to
  • A product trio culture: engineering, product and design as co-owners, outcomes over outputs
  • Competitive compensation that reflects the Staff level of this role
  • Training and conference budget, 30 days of vacation, modern equipment, mobility offers and a company pension plan
  • Hybrid work with 2–3 office days per week in Berlin, Munich, Pforzheim or Stockholm

How we hire

Remote, with feedback within 48 hours after every step:

1. 30-minute intro call with our Recruiter Mirko
2. 60-minute technical interview with our VP Engineering (your future manager) and an engineering lead: one frontend modernization you led, your design-system story, and how you use AI day to day
3. Case study: a hands-on part (AI tools explicitly welcome – walk us through how you used them) and a 45-minute architecture session
4. Team panel and a 45-minute conversation with our CPTO – optionally on site

FAQ

Is this a people-management role? No. It's a senior individual-contributor role: you lead through architecture, standards and enablement, without direct reports.

Who will I report to? Our VP Engineering. The role is sponsored by our CPTO: the frontend platform is one of the CPTO's top priorities, you agree the target architecture and migration roadmap together, and the CPTO holds your final interview.

Which tech stack will I work with? React and TypeScript on both products. FactFinder NG runs on a Java backend, Infinity on .NET/F# (with Fable/Feliz on the frontend). Backend, F# and our search domain are things you can learn here – React expertise, Web Components, design-system architecture and AI-first practice are what you bring from day one.

Is "AI-first" real here, or a buzzword? It's driven by our CPTO and part of the career ladder for every engineer. Your mandate is to take it from individual productivity to organization-wide practice.

Two legacy frontends on Java and .NET – isn't that painful? That's exactly the mandate: unify them, and how is your call. Incremental, not big-bang.

Can I work fully remote? No – the role is hybrid with 2–3 office days per week at one of our offices.

Why eCommerce search? Because agentic commerce is where AI meets real purchase decisions – on our platform that's 2,000+ shops and €160+ billion in GMV a year.

Apply

Send us your CV or LinkedIn profile plus links to work you're proud of (GitHub, a design system, a talk, a blog post) – and tell us in three sentences how you use AI in your daily engineering work. No cover letter needed.

Your contact: Mirko Duus

Prosus is repositioning itself as one global technology company, not a collection of investments and live experience plays an increasingly important role. And presence - to decide how and where Prosus turns up at the industry’s events (HumanX, SXSW, RAISE), and make each appearance feel deliberate and distinctly Prosus rather than another logo on a sponsor wall.

The role crosses brand, production, and storytelling. The right person thinks like a brand strategist, plans like a producer.

  • Own the experience and creative concept for Prosus’s flagship events — Luminate, Forward, and what comes next - from the idea to the room.

Brand in the Physical World

  • Bring the outside in: keep a sharp read on how the best in tech, culture, and luxury are building experiences, and raise Prosus’s game accordingly.

Delivery & Partners

  • Run the producer’s craft: budgets, timelines, vendors, venues, and flawless execution under pressure.

  • Keep global events consistent across markets: Europe, the US, China, Latin America without losing what makes each land locally.

  • Experience shaping how a brand shows up at major industry moments, not just running a booth.

Capabilities

Backgrounds We’d Love

Mindset

Not Required But Valued

jobs.description:
At Vio we believe booking accommodation should feel smart, fair, and effortless — never overwhelming or unclear.

As one of the world’s fastest-growing travel tech platforms, we help millions of users make smarter travel decisions by comparing stays across 100+ booking sites — so they can find the perfect place, at the best price, anywhere in the world. We cut through the noise and complexity of hotel and vacation rental booking, surfacing real value with clarity, transparency, and full support. No tricks. No confusion. Just great stays — booked with confidence. With operations in 100+ markets and growing fast, our mission is to reshape how people discover and book accommodation through technology travelers can trust.

Who we're looking for

We are looking for a hands-on Quality Platform Lead to own Vio's quality strategy and automation platform across web, mobile, browser extensions, internal tooling and related surfaces.

This is a technical leadership role (Staff IC) reporting to the Director of Engineering. You define what good looks like for quality, decide where scarce testing effort goes, and give teams the confidence to ship. Your levers are release gates, quality telemetry, and a developer experience that makes the right tests easy to write and keep alive.

Product engineers own the tests for the features they build. Your remit is the platform, the strategy and the enablement that make that work hold up at scale. There is no QA department here and we have no plans to create one.

Where you'll start

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

  • Web: Playwright, Checkly, BrowserStack

  • Mobile: Patrol (Flutter)

  • Coverage gaps across white-labels, browser extensions, widgets, APIs and internal tooling

The tooling can stay as it is. With a clear case you can migrate or rebuild. E2E coverage today is thin, so a different platform is genuinely on the table if it serves speed, maintainability and DX better. We have no predefined answer.

AI-assisted tooling is an open area too. We have no established practice for agent-generated tests or AI-assisted triage, so your judgment on what earns a place in the platform carries real weight.

What we lack today is clear ownership of strategy, release gates and shared quality telemetry, plus a low-friction path for engineers to spend their testing effort on the highest-risk scenarios.

How the role works

Your time splits between hands-on platform work, enablement, strategy and stakeholder telemetry. One insourced QA Engineer supports you. You own the technical direction, the standards and the quality outcomes.

Once the platform has low friction, product engineers write and maintain the tests for the domains they own. You enable that through patterns, docs, reusable modules, CI checks and risk-based guidance. Gatekeeping releases sits outside the role.

Expect no direct people-management responsibilities in the near future. Any further QE hire gets evaluated against the ~1:50 rule once the value is proven, and we have no committed headcount plan beyond that.

What you'll own

Quality strategy and platform

  • Own the quality strategy and the automation platform across products, covering direction, standards and day-to-day health

  • Decide whether to keep, evolve or replace the current tooling, with clear trade-offs on speed, maintainability and DX

  • Set coding standards and patterns for test code, and keep the suite focused on the tests that earn their place

Release gates and telemetry

  • Build automated release gates into CI/CD and define what protects the core journeys

  • Give Product, Engineering and leadership real-time quality telemetry on release readiness, risk and pipeline health

  • Put failure triage and flaky-test quarantine in place, so every failure is worth acting on

Risk-based coverage and testability

  • Work with Product and Engineering to protect high-impact journeys and APIs

  • Retire flaky and low-value tests, and concentrate effort where the risk is highest

  • Act as the technical stakeholder for testability (hooks, mocks, contract tests, test data) and get those improvements onto team roadmaps

Developer enablement

  • Make it easy for product engineers to write, run and maintain tests locally and in CI

  • Embed quality into how teams plan and ship, and mentor the insourced QA Engineer

  • Drive a measurable increase in developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX

What success looks like in 12 months

  1. Platform ownership. You have taken over the automation platform across products and own it outright, with direction, standards and health all unambiguous, whether you kept the tooling or replaced it.

  2. Gates and focus. Release gates on the core journeys are fast and deterministic, and testing effort sits on the highest-risk scenarios.

  3. Dev ownership and satisfaction. Writing and maintaining tests is a routine part of Definition of Done, and developer satisfaction with quality tooling and DX has measurably improved.

  4. Telemetry. Eng and Product work from live release-readiness and risk dashboards, failures triage cleanly, and flaky tests go into quarantine.

  5. Less manual drag. Regular releases go out without manual testing, with exploratory testing reserved for major new work.

Who you are

  • You have a track record of building or overhauling automation platforms (SWE / QE / SDET)

  • You write production-grade code across app, test and infra repos. Language matters less to us than depth, though our stack today leans on TypeScript/JS, Elixir, Go, Python and Dart.

  • You use AI agents effectively in your own engineering workflow and can judge where they belong inside a quality platform, from test generation to failure triage

  • You have cross-platform web and mobile automation judgment, and can weigh unified toolchains against separate ones objectively

  • You have deep CI/CD and test infrastructure experience: GitHub Actions, device clouds, parallelisation, test data

  • You can translate quality risk into telemetry and decisions that Eng, Product and leadership act on

  • You are a hands-on builder who wants to code the platform yourself

  • You design platforms developers adopt, and you prioritise risk-based coverage

Trade-offs we accept: depth on one platform when the other is learnable, and no travel or booking domain background.

Why join us now?

  • Full ownership of the quality strategy and the automation platform, with a mandate for enablement

  • We are one of the most innovative and fastest-growing accommodation booking platforms in the world today, having grown our bookings 30x between 2017 and 2025, and catering to the needs of over 100 million unique visitors worldwide each year. We do that by harnessing the power of advanced algorithms and an innovative suite of power features and managed to overcome the corona crisis remarkably fast;

  • The mobile applications (iOS and Android) we launched in 2023 are already a big success, reaching 5 million installs with great customer reviews, as we are beginning to build Vio as the brand for value-seeking travellers worldwide;

  • We are a passionate and diverse team of tech enthusiasts and creatives with a commitment and focus on the traveler above all else - and it shows in our industry-leading TrustPilot score;

  • We place huge importance on rewarding our employees for the value they generate by giving Stock Appreciation Rights to all employees.

Do you want to know if Vio is the right place for you? Find out by reading about the attitude that thrives at Vio.

What we offer:

  • Plenty of chances to learn and grow within an open, diverse culture which promotes knowledge sharing, trust and transparency;

  • A great compensation package, perks and benefits (including significant stock appreciation rights);

  • Flexible time off (take as many holidays as you need) and a chance to work remotely;

  • You will be part of a highly international team that enjoys working, eating and playing together in one of the best office locations in Amsterdam;

  • We value good food and offer catered lunches from various cuisines, great coffee, and the occasional barbecue in our garden;

  • We enjoy getting together to celebrate our wins with company events in Amsterdam and abroad;

  • A budget for your dream home office;

  • Access to free mental health support via OpenUp.

jobs.title: Site Development Program Manager
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.


BY JOINING OUR TEAM YOU’LL GET TO

  • Build the machine that builds the machine. Join TechOps at the forefront of advanced manufacturing, we’re building the production system that will enable commercial fusion. The Production lines, tooling, and processes are being developed from the ground up; you'll create the ways of working, not inherit them.

  • Work at the frontier of manufacturing technology. Bring your creativity to evaluate, qualify, and deploy processes with no industry playbook, every component you build and every process you shape goes directly into the core of the stellarator magnet technology.

  • Do work that matters, and see it grow. The hardware you build is the product and your career grows with it, from prototyping and process development through quality and industrialization, alongside exceptional colleagues from around the world.

  • Make an impact you can point to. In a small, fast-moving team, your calls on equipment, quality, and process directly shape how a world-class deep-tech company produces superconducting magnets with results visible on the shop floor, not buried in a slidedeck.

YOUR IMPACT

You'll hold Proxima Fusion's site development portfolio together as one program, spanning projects such as Stellaris, our manufacturing and testing infrastructure, and other site development work. Working closely with the project managers who lead each project, you'll make sure feasibility, key partner relationships and permitting strategy are handled coherently across the portfolio. Without this role, projects risk optimizing for themselves while the issues that cut across them fall through the gaps.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Lead Proxima Fusion's site development program across multiple parallel projects, owning feasibility, key partner and stakeholder relationships, and permitting strategy

  • Work closely with the project managers leading each site, aligning their schedules, budgets and deliverables to a single program roadmap

  • Define and run the program's decision-gate structure, from initial project approval through to final investment decision, including deliverables, readiness levels, and cost and schedule tracking

  • Represent Proxima Fusion to site owners, utility partners and other key stakeholders, building constructive, diplomatic partnerships across sites with different contexts and regulatory histories

  • Own the permitting landscape across the portfolio, including radiation protection law, environmental permitting, building permits and other approvals where relevant, and sequence parallel approval processes into one coherent strategy

  • Build organizational and infrastructure scaling plans that look beyond near-term needs, from initial capacity towards multi-GW scale

  • Report program status, risks and key decisions to senior leadership

WHO YOU ARE

  • Extensive experience leading greenfield or brownfield energy or industrial site development programs through to final investment decision, ideally on former or adjacent nuclear sites or other heavily regulated sites

  • A track record of managing multiple projects in parallel at different stages of maturity, using a structured, gate-based approach

  • Skilled at building productive relationships with incumbent site owners and utilities, and comfortable working within formal, process-driven stakeholder cultures

  • Able to pull together detailed technical requirements from engineers and specialists without needing a deep engineering background yourself

  • Fluent in German and English, which the regulatory and stakeholder landscape requires

  • Comfortable building program structure from scratch in a fast-scaling, first-of-a-kind environment

    INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

At Proxima Fusion, our mission is bold: making limitless clean energy a reality. To get there, we need a high-performing, diverse team that brings different perspectives, challenges assumptions, and builds together with purpose. We know that diversity of thought and experience leads to better ideas, stronger execution, and a more resilient team. We don’t look at how you identify, what you look like, who you choose to worship or what ethnicity you are. We care about what you can bring to the table.

Most importantly, you want to prove that AI can be trusted with people’s money.

What You’ll Own

What you build will decide how far Aspora goes beyond payments, and how fast we get there.

Why Aspora

jobs.title: Program Manager – Ecosystem Strategy & Operations
jobs.description:
Who We Are

You've ordered dinner through Just Eat Takeaway. You've bought and sold on OLX. You've paid with PayU. Chances are, you've already used a Prosus company today.

We are Prosus, a global technology company powering some of the world's leading lifestyle ecommerce businesses. Every day, billions of people across India, Latin America, Europe and beyond use our products and services to buy, sell, pay, connect and discover.

Our AI-driven ecosystem spans 100+ companies across ecommerce, food delivery, fintech and experiences, serving billions of consumers worldwide. AI powers how we operate and innovate, with more than 60,000 active AI agents helping our teams build, scale and move faster. Through our investment team, we also back the founders and technologies shaping the future: From robotics and autonomous systems to synthetic biology and frontier AI.

Guided by our five values Innovation, Results, People, Impact, and Entrepreneurship, culture is our competitive advantage. We thrive with experimentation; we build, we test, we learn, we iterate.

Join us in shaping the future of technology at global scale.

The Opportunity

We’re looking for a Program Manager to join the Prosus team in Amsterdam. This is a unique opportunity to sit at the heart of one of the most ambitious AI agendas in the consumer internet industry, driving the execution of our flagship AI programs across a portfolio of companies that reach hundreds of millions of users worldwide. You’ll be the connective tissue between strategy and delivery — turning the AI team’s priorities into structured programs, keeping senior stakeholders aligned, and making sure the most important initiatives ship on time and at quality. If you enjoy operating in a fast-moving, high-visibility environment where your work directly shapes how AI is built and deployed across iFood, OLX, PayU, Stack Overflow and other Prosus brands, you’ll thrive here.

Who You Are

You’re a builder of operating systems, not a meeting scheduler. You take ambiguous, high-stakes initiatives and turn them into clear plans, owners, milestones and decisions. You’re comfortable holding senior leaders accountable to commitments, and you have the judgment to know when to push, when to escalate, and when to absorb noise so others can focus. You move with the speed of a startup and the rigor of a top-tier consulting firm — structured thinking, sharp written communication, and a bias for action. You’re energized by working across cultures and time zones, equally at ease in a room of engineers debating product strategy and in a boardroom-level review with C-level executives. Above all, you’re curious about AI and excited to help shape how it transforms billion-user businesses.

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of experience in program management, strategy & operations, management consulting, chief-of-staff or comparable cross-functional roles, ideally within tech, AI, or fast-scaling consumer internet businesses.

  • Proven ability to run complex, multi-stakeholder programs end-to-end — from defining objectives and OKRs through to delivery, governance and reporting to senior leadership.

  • Strong structured thinking and written communication: you can take a messy problem and produce a clear narrative, a sharp deck, or a concise briefing for an executive audience.

  • Experience working directly with senior leaders (C-level or equivalent), with the maturity and presence to challenge, push back, and drive decisions when needed.

  • Comfort operating across cultures and time zones, with a track record of building trust with technical and non-technical teams across multiple geographies.

  • Genuine curiosity about AI and its application to consumer products — you don’t need to be a researcher, but you should be fluent enough to engage meaningfully with product, engineering and data science teams.

  • English Fluency

  • Willingness to be based in Amsterdam, with regular travel to portfolio companies across Europe, Latin America and India

Your Typical Day

You start the day catching up with program leads across time zones — a quick sync with the Life Assistants team in São Paulo, a check-in on LLM milestones, a review of where the week’s OKRs stand. Mid-morning, you’re in a working session with the AI leadership team, pressure-testing a decision before it goes to the EVP. By midday you’re drafting a one-page briefing for an upcoming board update, distilling complex program status into the three things that matter. In the afternoon, you facilitate a Monthly Review Meeting with a portfolio company, capture decisions and follow-ups, and unblock two cross-team dependencies before they slip. You close the day prepping the agenda for tomorrow’s leadership offsite and sending a sharp end-of-day note to keep stakeholders aligned.

Why Prosus?

At Prosus, your colleagues include 60,000 AI agents… and your job is to figure out what that actually means. We're one of the largest operators of agentic AI on the planet, inside a $100B+ portfolio across 100+ companies and two billion people. The humans here own what AI can't do alone: judgment, creativity, and the call on what gets built next.

Own the impact. Work the ecosystem. Earn your growth. Build with backing.

Curious about our perks and benefits? Take a look at this page.

Our Diversity & Inclusion Commitment

We respect the dignity and human rights of individuals and communities wherever we operate in the world. Building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels welcome and can thrive is critical for us. We provide access to education, which helps everyone understand the important role they play and the positive impact they can have.

Refractal is an AI security company building the infrastructure organisations need to defend against autonomous AI threats. 2026 has shown that generally capable intelligence is here. Refractal was founded on cybersecurity and AI expertise from MIT, Microsoft, NASA and the U.S. Navy. Our product lets organisations detect AI-enabled threats at low cost without sacrificing detection quality. We take a practical approach to AI risk, combining proven cybersecurity methods with frontier AI security research.

Today, we work with governments and organisations that can't afford to get security wrong. We're backed by leading deep-tech and cybersecurity investors and are growing the team to deliver on this mission.

The role

You'll lead product design at Refractal, covering the operator console, policy authoring, investigation and audit views, and the design system behind them. Your work will shape how security, risk and compliance teams find and respond to AI threats.

  • Design core workflows, including policy authoring, real-time triage, investigations and audit reporting.

Nice to have

  • Design experience on security, observability or compliance products.

  • Front-end prototyping in code.

Our values

Radical transparency. We believe the best work happens when everyone feels able to give and receive honest, constructive feedback.

Public service. We see AI security as a form of public service. Getting the AI transition right means putting the right infrastructure in place to manage the threats that come with it, and our work helps protect the institutions and services society depends on.

Fail fast. We test ideas early, seek feedback and learn quickly. We experiment rapidly and change course when something isn't working, without compromising on security.

Pragmatism, not dogmatism. We choose approaches based on how well they solve the problem. That means combining established cybersecurity methods with frontier AI research, questioning our assumptions, and changing our minds when the evidence changes.

À propos de Pennylane

Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen.

 

En 6 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à :

💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant

Role context

Pennylane currently operates around 50,000 business accounts through a BaaS model with Swan and is applying for Établissement de paiement and Société de financement licences. As we prepare to onboard new customers under our own licensed entity from mid-2027, we are building our first line of defence across onboarding, transaction monitoring, fraud and risk operations.

As Transaction Monitoring & Fraud Operations Lead, you will be one of the first operational leaders in this greenfield setup. Reporting to the Head of FinCrime Operations, you will lead first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations across Pennylane’s payment activities within a single team. You will own first-line alert handling and fraud case management, with clear escalation paths to Compliance and Risk.

Your mission will be to build and launch Pennylane’s first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations, then scale the team and its workflows as volumes grow—while maintaining strong decision quality, auditability and customer protection.

This is a high-autonomy role with direct exposure to a strategic regulatory project and close collaboration with Product, Compliance and Risk. You will help shape how Pennylane protects the financial activity of French SMEs as it brings more of its regulated operations in-house.

Responsibilities

  • Own end-to-end first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for business customers, ensuring that alert triage, investigations, customer outreach and escalations are completed in line with policies set by Compliance and Risk and within agreed SLAs.

  • Translate AML/CFT and fraud policies into operational procedures, decision trees and analyst playbooks, and provide evidence-based recommendations on alert quality and operational bottlenecks.

  • Review complex or high-risk alerts within the first-line mandate, oversee post-onboarding fraud cases and ensure that escalations, customer complaints and law-enforcement requests are handled with complete, auditable records.

  • Implement the QA and reporting framework, monitor operational and risk indicators, and support Compliance during controls testing, audits and regulatory reviews.

  • Recruit, onboard and lead the transaction monitoring and fraud analyst team, combining hands-on support with effective coaching and a culture of rigour, accountability and continuous learning.

  • Establish the team’s performance and capacity framework, covering SLAs, productivity, quality, backlogs, false-positive rates and hiring needs.

  • Partner with Product and Tech to test and improve transaction-monitoring, fraud and back-office workflows, prioritising automation while identifying the controls and decisions that should remain manual.

First 6–12 months

  • Deliver approved operating procedures, analyst playbooks and escalation rules before go-live.

  • Establish a capacity and hiring plan based on observed alert volumes and handling times.

  • Validate that alert queues, evidence collection, account measures and second-line handovers work operationally before launch.

  • By go-live, have first-line monitoring operational for new customers, with trained coverage, agreed SLAs, documented QA controls and named escalation owners.

What we’re looking for

  • Significant experience in transaction monitoring, fraud or broader financial-crime operations within a regulated financial-services environment, including ownership of operational performance and complex case decisions.

  • Proven experience leading and developing an operational team responsible for alert queues or investigations, combining effective coaching with a hands-on player-coach approach when needed.

  • Strong understanding of first-line alert handling: triage, investigation, typology, escalation, and the difference between a fraud case and an AML case.

  • Good working knowledge of French and European AML/CFT expectations, including ACPR and TRACFIN requirements, and experience translating policy into SOPs, decision trees and analyst guidance.

  • Experience working with Product or Tech on workflow or tooling changes.

  • Sound judgement on what to automate, what to sample and what to escalate.

  • Ability to use operational metrics to manage quality, backlogs and capacity.

  • Ability to make structured, well-documented decisions under pressure and communicate complex cases clearly to operational and compliance stakeholders.

  • Comfort building operations in a greenfield environment where volumes are still uncertain and tooling is evolving.

  • Exposure to ACPR expectations, a licensing programme, a BaaS migration or law-enforcement requests would be an advantage.

Languages, presence and location

  • Fluent French and English are mandatory.

  • Based in France, with a strong preference for Paris.

  • Regular on-site presence in Paris is expected. Partial remote is possible. This is not a fully remote role.

Why join

  • Build first-line transaction monitoring and fraud operations for a new regulated entity from the ground up.

  • Shape the operating model before launch, rather than inheriting fixed processes and tooling.

  • Take ownership of a critical domain with a direct impact on go-live readiness, customer protection and responsible growth.

jobs.title: Web Developer (all genders)
jobs.description:
Your creative field

We are looking for a full-time, permanent Web Developer (all genders) to start as soon as possible. We live remote-first within Germany, but you have the freedom to choose whether you want to work hybrid or completely on-site due to your proximity to one of our locations.


What makes a good web developer? Not just that they code beautifully – but that they also know everything is still running at 3 a.m. Here, you work according to the "you build it, you run it" principle: full ownership, a modern tech stack, and AI-assisted development that lets you actively shape the architecture of our website.

That's exactly who we're looking for. Not a developer who hands off their code and then watches what happens to it, but someone who builds it, runs it, and stands behind it. For us, "you build it, you run it" isn't a saying that sounds nice – it's everyday reality:
 you write a feature, test it, push it live, and if something wobbles afterward, you're the one who sets it straight again. Not because no one else is around, but because you know best what you built. No blame game, no ticket disappearing into another team's queue, no "that's not my problem anymore" – real ownership, from the first commit to stable operation in production.

What does that look like in practice? On a typical day, you work on new features for our website, often supported by AI-assisted, agentic coding – not as a gimmick, but as a completely normal tool in your everyday work. You exchange ideas with the team, bring your own thinking to the architecture, and help make decisions rather than just implementing specs. You deploy through continuous delivery, keep an eye on how your code behaves in production, and when something isn't running smoothly, you dig into it yourself instead of waiting for someone else to.

You work with a modern stack (Astro, SvelteKit, TypeScript) and have the freedom to actively shape the architecture of our website – not as a bystander, but as someone whose fingerprints are visible in the end result. We're not interested in celebrating process for its own sake; what matters to us is that good ideas find their way into production quickly: short paths, a lot of trust, and little bureaucracy.


What convinces us

Your personality, paired with: 

  • 3–5 years of hands-on experience in web development (agency or in-house)
  • Strong, proven expertise with Astro, SvelteKit (SSG & SSR) and TypeScript
  • Experience with headless CMS (ideally PayloadCMS), Git and CI/CD pipelines (GitLab)
  • Hands-on experience with agentic coding tools (e.g. Claude, OpenCode) and an AI-forward mindset
  • Fluent German and English
  • IT-related education/degree or equivalent practical experience
  • A "you build it, you run it" mentality, paired with strong ownership and reliability
  • Strong analytical skills, clear goal- and results-orientation, and a genuine customer-first mindset
  • Team spirit, strong communication skills, and openness to change
  • Nice to have: Kubernetes, Docker, agile development processes, and terminal power-user skills (Neovim, tmux)
 
 
We know that you may not currently meet all the requirements. But if you come to us with the right amount of commitment and enthusiasm, we can take off together and make a big difference.


Awesome Prospects

At Contabo, we are constantly evolving. Our growth creates space for new ideas, ownership, and real impact for people who want to make a difference.
What defines us is trust, direct communication, and an open feedback culture. We believe the best solutions are built together and that everyone has the opportunity to contribute, grow, and leave their own footprint.

Additionally, we offer:

  • Work the way that fits your life – Remote or hybrid with flexible hours for a healthy work-life balance and the same technical equipment at home as in the office
  • Experience real freedom – Workation across the EU and in our summer office in Mallorca
  • Stay active and healthy – Access to EGYM Wellpass and thousands of fitness and wellness facilities
  • Enjoy exclusive perks – Attractive discounts on many products and services through our corporate benefits program
  • Recharge your energy – 30 days of vacation plus additional days off on Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve
  • Give back – An extra day off to get involved in social activities through our Volunteer Day
  • Make an impact – Take ownership and bring your ideas to life with real creative freedom
  • Keep growing – Individual professional and personal development opportunities in an innovative tech environment
  • Feel comfortable where you work – Modern, conveniently located offices across our European locations
  • Be part of a diverse team – Work in an international environment shaped by diversity
  • Create lasting memories – Company events and team activities you won’t forget


How to reach us

If you have any questions, you can reach out to Alina by phone +49 89 2441067714.

jobs.title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile.

We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue.

We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance.

This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading.

The Role

RevenueCat helps apps of all shapes and sizes make more money across mobile, the web, and a growing list of other platforms like Roku, Amazon, and even AR through support for Vision Pro. As a result, many different types of users log in and use RevenueCat on a day-to-day basis. Product managers, support reps, lifecycle marketers, user acquisition specialists, data analysts, executives: the list goes on.

Communicating the growing breadth of use cases supported by RevenueCat in a way that makes sense for all those different types of businesses, apps, and users is a challenge. And that’s where product marketing comes in.

We’re looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our growing Product Marketing team led by Francie. Each Senior PMM owns a product area end-to-end, partnering with that area's product managers on positioning, messaging, and go-to-market. This is not a segment-specific role: RevenueCat serves everyone from solo indie developers to top-tier enterprise apps, often through the very same product surface, so you'll craft messaging and channels that flex across that full spectrum. This role is perfect for someone who:

  • Knows APIs and SDKs like their ABCs. Code may not be your craft, but you know how to talk the talk. Software developers are one of our core audiences, and they can smell BS a mile away. You can debug marketing messaging so it resonates with technical audiences, and craft narratives around the 1’s and 0’s that still land with business stakeholders.

  • Captains their own ship. You have a strong bias toward action and you’re not afraid to get your hands dirty on execution. Whether it’s juggling strategic and tactical work or navigating shifting priorities, you thrive on autonomy and love making things happen.

  • Distills collaborative chaos. You’re comfortable raising your hand and getting what you need from a dynamic and technical organization. Whether it’s nudging engineers for product updates or rallying Sales for customer stories, you can navigate the chaos and advocate for what the GTM org needs.

  • Gets excited about the unexpected. At RevenueCat we take shipping seriously, and are constantly adapting our product and strategies to meet the needs of developers. You see changes in direction and shifts in strategy as an opportunity to flex your creative muscles and learn on the fly.

  • Is a little quirky. You love a whimsical side quest and you can see the soft side of software. We pride ourselves in keeping our community on their toes with unique swag, challenges and events. You can play as big a role as you’d like in helping to brainstorm and bring these quirky concepts to life.

What You’ll Be Responsible For

  • GTM and adoption campaigns: Own key product areas to deeply understand the features we’re launching and the use cases and needs behind them. Craft compelling communication plans both within the organization, and to existing and prospective customers.

  • Lifecycle campaign building: Working with our marketing operations team to execute insight-based lifecycle campaigns to drive adoption, retention and community.

  • Web page design and optimization: Translate product messaging and customer understanding into visually compelling and highly converting web experiences with the help of our external web development agency. You’ll chart the vision for the story our website tells and the illustrations, animations and tools we create to convey it.

  • Case studies and testimonials: Organizing, facilitating, and translating customer interviews into compelling case studies and testimonials that showcase the value of RevenueCat.

  • Internal enablement: As an expert in your areas of product focus, you’ll empower developer-facing teams with the resources and training they need to support developers and ensure their success.

  • Market insights: Keeping your finger on the pulse of the mobile app industry and competitors to inform go-to-market strategies and uncover new opportunities for growth.

  • Whimsical side quests: Taking on unique projects with minimal instruction, coordinating the collection of 1000 screenshots to launch Paywalls.com, designing, printing and shipping a calendar of cat photos, hosting the World Paywall Speed Building Championships, or crafting a keynote speech for leadership. You’ll get to work on projects that stretch your creative muscles.

What You’ll Need to Be Successful

  • 5+ years of experience in Product Marketing within a B2B or B2D SaaS environment, preferably targeting developers or software companies. RevenueCat runs a hybrid motion - self-serve/PLG for indie developers alongside a sales-assisted motion for larger accounts - so experience with either end of that spectrum is valuable; you won't need to have done both to succeed here.

  • Previous experience as a solo-marketer is preferred. While you’ll have the broader marketing and product marketing teams to lean on, our async, entrepreneurial culture is best suited to someone who is comfortable independently driving projects forward, making progress amid changing processes, and actively enlisting cross-functional support when needed.

  • Experience owning end-to-end go-to-market efforts, including tier 1 product launches. Strong project management skills to prioritize multiple initiatives and execute effectively across teams.

  • Strong creative instincts and direction. You’ve led the charge on web design work and aren’t afraid to sketch, prototype in Figma, or use AI tools to get to an ugly starting point. Comfortable collaborating with external creative agencies and freelancers to deliver high-quality assets.

  • Excellent editorial judgment: you understand audience, tone, and communication objectives, and you can elevate copy through clear direction and feedback. You will not need to write everything yourself, but you’re comfortable jumping in to draft a narrative outline or even a blog post when necessary, and you know when to pass work forward to the content team or a technical writer

  • Exceptional communication skills to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams, ensuring alignment and buy-in from key stakeholders.

  • A proven ability to translate complex technical concepts into compelling messaging that resonates with different audiences, both internally and externally.

  • The resourcefulness to take on unique, sometimes ambiguous projects that require initiative and problem-solving.

Ideally you:

  • Have experience in the mobile app ecosystem or working with subscription-based software products.

  • Have worked in an early-stage tech company or led new initiatives independently in a larger organization.

  • Have experience working as a solo marketer or solo PMM within an organization.

  • Are comfortable with tools like Notion, Slack, Zoom, and Linear for remote collaboration.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first month, you’ll:

  • Gain hands-on experience with the RevenueCat platform, supported by our engineers and advocates.

  • Build a foundational understanding of the app ecosystem, particularly around monetization.

  • Establish relationships with key collaborators across Product, Sales, and Marketing.

  • Deliver your “first ship,” a project that demonstrates your insights and adds real value to the team.

Within the first 3 months, you’ll:

  • Step into the role as the go-to-market owner for your specific product areas, becoming an expert on relevant features, their roadmap and related market segments.

  • Own the go-to-market efforts for product areas, leading cross-functional teams to ensure successful execution of awareness and adoption efforts.

  • Craft and distribute internal enablement materials and training related to your product areas.

  • Publish a new landing page, leading the concept, briefing, design and written copy process, with execution by our web agency.

  • Conduct customer research to deepen your understanding of our audience’s challenges and goals, and publish a customer case study.

Within the first 6 months, you’ll:

  • Own and optimize the self-serve adoption funnel for your product areas, partnering with Growth and Product and leveraging lifecycle marketing to turn feature interest into activation and long-term retention.

  • Level up your product area’s sales motion by revamping core pitch materials, competitive positioning, and objection handling.

  • Partner with Product to translate customer and market insights into clear roadmap recommendations.

  • Contribute to a whimsical side quest that adds to our brand and community.

After 12 months, you’ll:

  • Be a trusted partner across Product, Sales, and Marketing, contributing strategically to RevenueCat’s growth.

  • Have led multiple successful product launches, including a tier 1 launch, and owned key marketing initiatives.

  • Represent RevenueCat at industry events and conferences

  • Deepen your knowledge of app development and monetization, becoming an expert in the space.

What we offer:

  • Competitive equity in a fast-growing, Series C startup backed by top-tier investors, including Y Combinator

  • 10-year window to exercise vested equity options

  • A fully remote environment designed around autonomy and flexibility

  • 4-5 weeks of flexible time off annually

  • Paid desk at a co-working space

  • Workspace budget and continuous learning stipend

Interviewing at RevenueCat

Our interview process is rigorous on purpose. We want to be sure that everyone we bring on is genuinely excited about this work, aligned with how we operate, and ready to meet our high bar for performance. Curious what that actually looks like? Read more in our blog post on how we hire at RevenueCat, including tips to help you succeed.

jobs.description:

Patronus entwickelt intelligente Notruf-Technologie, die Senior*innen mehr Sicherheit und Unabhängigkeit im Alltag gibt. Mehr als 25.000 Menschen verlassen sich bereits auf uns. Was uns als Team ausmacht: schnelle Entscheidungswege, viel Eigenverantwortung und echter Gestaltungsspielraum.

Deine Mission

  • Führung & Coaching: Das Product-Management-Team führen, durch regelmäßige 1:1s individuell fördern und optimale Rahmenbedingungen für eine erfolgreiche Zusammenarbeit schaffen.

  • Strategie & Roadmap: Produktstrategie und übergreifende Roadmap für Web, Mobile und Platform verantworten, Prioritäten setzen und dabei Geschäftsziele sowie Teamkapazitäten in Einklang bringen.

  • Datengetriebene Entscheidungen: User Behavior, KPIs und Nutzerfeedback analysieren, Hypothesen ableiten und validieren.

  • Prozesse & UX: Komplexe: Kundenprozesse in durchdachte Workflows und herausragende User Experience übersetzen.

  • Strategie & Stakeholder: Gemeinsam mit dem CTPO die Produktstrategie gestalten und als Brücke zwischen Stakeholdern, Engineering und QA agieren.

  • AI & Agentic Development: AI-gestütztes Prototyping und UI-Generierung im Alltag nutzen und agentische Arbeitsweisen im gesamten Product-Team etablieren – von Discovery über Spec-Erstellung bis Testing.

Dein Talent

  • Fundierte Führungserfahrung im Product Management, bestenfalls im Start-up-Umfeld mit schnellen Iterationen, wechselnden Anforderungen und echtem Gestaltungsspielraum

Unser Angebot

jobs.title: Performance Marketer (Paid Ads + Creative)
jobs.description:
Data quality is the bottleneck of the AI era. Every Fortune 500 is trying to solve it. We're the team they call.

Soda is the data quality layer for Disney, Ralph Lauren, CBRE, HelloFresh, 2K Games, and Nubank. Our open-source engine, Soda Core, is used by companies like Tesla, Slack, Adyen, Walmart, and JPMC. The category is growing fast because AI doesn't work on bad data.

We're hiring one person to own paid acquisition end to end.

About Us

Soda's mission is to monitor the world's decisions. We're building the first Data & AI performance monitoring platform that spans data collection to automated decision-making.

The Role

Not to manage an agency. Not to approve creative someone else made. You write the ad, you make the asset, you build the landing page, you launch it, you own the budget, and you read the numbers on Monday and kill what didn't work.

You'll join the Growth team reporting to a co-founder.

What you might call yourself. Performance marketer, paid media manager, paid acquisition lead, demand gen manager, growth marketer, creative strategist, media buyer, or the person at a startup who just ended up running the ads. We don't care what's on your CV. You need to have run B2B paid yourself and you need to have made the creative, and most people have only done one.

Who this is for. People who have personally run enterprise B2B ads at a company nobody had heard of yet. You know what a $40 click feels like, you know why the creative that won on LinkedIn dies on Reddit, and you have opinions about it that you earned by losing money that mattered.

If your last job was allocating budget across channels and reviewing what an agency shipped, this isn't it. If you've been making the ads yourself because it was faster than briefing someone, this is it.

What You'll Do

  • Own paid acquisition end to end: LinkedIn, Meta, Google, Reddit, , ChatGpt, X, and whatever you can prove works.
  • Make the creative. Copy, static, video, landing pages. You are the studio, and AI is how you get to twenty variants instead of two.
  • Run a real testing cadence: hypothesis, ship, read, kill. Volume of tests is the job; most of them will lose and that's the point.
  • Own the budget and the number. Pipeline and qualified meetings, not impressions.
  • Work with the founders, customer engineers, and customers on what Soda actually says to the market. Your opinion matters here.

Requirements

  • You've run enterprise B2B paid at a startup or growth-stage technical company: data, infrastructure, developer tools, security, or observability. Long cycles, a buying committee, high contract values - and no brand pull to coast on. Running paid for a company everyone has heard of, with a big budget and an agency, is a different job to running it for one nobody knows yet on a budget that doesn't forgive waste. We need the second one.
  • Experiment obsessed: the testing cadence is the job. Tell us how many tests you ran last quarter, the last five and what each one was trying to learn, which ones you were wrong about, and what you killed. Most of them should have lost.
  • You make the creative: send us ads you personally made, with what they cost and what they returned. The most important line in this ad.
  • AI-first: you use frontier models to produce and iterate creative at volume, and you can tell us specifically where AI made it better and where it made it worse.
  • You own the budget: you've had spend authority and hit a number with it.
  • Enough technical range to be unblocked: landing pages, tracking, conversion APIs, UTMs, a CRM. Nothing waits on an engineer.
  • Enough data fluency to be credible: you're selling to data engineers and CDOs. You don't have to be one, but you can't sound like you've never met one.
  • Clear written English: most of the job is words on a page that someone decides about in two seconds.

Good to Have

  • Data quality, data management, or data observability specifically.
  • You've built the attribution model as well as run the ads.
  • Founder or first-marketer background where nobody was going to do it for you.
  • You were the first paid hire somewhere and built the function from zero.

Benefits

  • Compensation: $120,000-$130,000 / €110,000-€120,000 per year + equity - the same band wherever you live. We don't discount for geography.
  • Fully remote (US or EU-based), with offices in Brooklyn.
  • All the tokens you need, across all frontier models.
  • Real budget, real ownership, no micromanagement.
  • Colleagues in 12+ countries, and the local equivalent of PTO, retirement, and medical cover.

Our Values

We value freedom with responsibility, transparency, and a growth mindset. We avoid politics, have no tolerance for dishonesty, and value open and direct communication without judgment. We proactively bring up and address potential issues before they become critical, and we overcommunicate frequently. Working at Soda, you will have full autonomy to make impactful decisions.

❤️ Why you will love to join Soda

  • Be part of a transformation: data quality is having its moment, and we're at the front of it.
  • Ownership from day one: if you see a bottleneck, you remove it.
  • International culture: colleagues in 12+ countries.
  • Work on your own terms: fully remote, flexible hours.
  • Paid the same wherever you are: one band for the US and Europe, no geographic discount.
  • You own a channel, not a task list: the paid function is yours to build from the ground up.
  • Budget to test with, and no committee between you and shipping an ad.

😡 What you might not love

  • Rapidly changing priorities: our roadmap can pivot quickly. It's a fast-paced environment with a LOT of work to be done.
  • Flexibility required: you will have to learn new things all the time.
  • No agency, no designer to hand things to: if you don't make it, it doesn't exist.
  • Judged on pipeline, not on the work: a beautiful campaign that sourced nothing is a failure.

Hiring Process

  1. 15-minute phone screen - with a founder
  2. Short assignment
  3. Craft deep dive (90 min)
  4. Culture fit (1 hour)

We answer every application, and every candidate hears back within 3-5 days of each step. If it's not a hell yes, it's a no, and we'll tell you quickly and kindly.

jobs.description:
About Mistral

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

The team

Mistral is building a sovereign AI cloud for Europe. Our customers in finance, healthcare, and the public sector run frontier models on European-jurisdiction infrastructure, and the Cloud Platform team builds the systems that make that possible — compute orchestration, Kubernetes, bare metal, storage, networking, and the datacenter fleet that runs it all.

We run it all on our own metal, our own network, our own datacenters — which means when something breaks, the fix is ours to write.

European Compute Units let enterprises commit to multi-year capacity on that infrastructure, and we are scaling toward a gigawatt of compute across Europe by 2030. You will design and ship the layer every sovereign AI deployment depends on and shape the team building it.

The Role

This is a people-leadership role from day one. You will manage the team — hiring, coaching, performance, growth paths, honest feedback — while staying close to the code: roughly half your time in architecture decisions and the hardest technical problems the team faces, the other half leading your squad. If you are looking for a senior IC role, this is not it.

You will lead the team building our serverless containers product: the way developers run AI apps, MCP servers, APIs, and managed workers on our cloud without thinking about servers. Push a container, get an endpoint, scale from zero to thousands of instances and back down — across CPU and GPU.

On a hyperscaler, the serverless layer is a product someone else built. Here you own it end to end: the scheduler that decides where a container lands, the routing path a request takes, the machinery that turns a scaled-to-zero service into a warm instance before a customer notices. All of it runs on metal, network, and datacenters we own.

That tension is the product: scale-to-zero economics with cold starts in milliseconds, autoscaling that absorbs a launch spike without a config change, GPUs scheduled onto containers the way other platforms schedule CPU. The customers betting on this layer are the developers building the next generation of AI software on European infrastructure.

What You Will Do

  • Own the container platform end to end: image delivery, placement, request routing, scale-up, scale-to-zero — across CPU and GPU.

  • Make cold starts a solved problem: snapshotting, prewarming, image-layer caching, whatever it takes for scale-from-zero to feel instant.

  • Treat AI workloads as the normal case: GPU-backed containers, streaming responses, long-lived connections, MCP servers that cost almost nothing while idle.

  • Write Go alongside your team and own the architecture and the hardest implementation decisions.

  • Grow the engineers, not just the software — set the standard for ownership and coach people past their comfort zone.

  • Own people management for the team: hiring, performance, growth paths, and honest feedback.

  • Partner with Product Managers to turn platform decisions into a product developers want to deploy on.

What We're Looking For

  • 2+ years of real people leadership. You have managed engineers — hired, coached, given honest feedback, and grown them. Hands-on contribution matters here, but this role is judged on the team you build and lead, not just the code you write.

  • You have shipped production systems in Go. Not dabbled. Shipped.

  • You have built container or workload platforms — orchestration, scheduling, isolation, request routing — not just deployed onto someone else's serverless platform.

  • Deep Linux: namespaces, cgroups, image layers, page cache — comfortable well below the application layer.

  • Multi-tenancy instincts: density, isolation, and fairness when hundreds of customers share one fleet.

Senior Customer Success Manager

As a Senior Customer Success Manager at DataSnipper, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring our customers achieve their goals using our innovative, AI-powered solutions. You will own the customer journey, from onboarding to driving long-term value and retention, fostering strong relationships built on trust and collaboration. This role offers a unique opportunity to work closely with professionals who are the backbone of global capital markets, deliver exceptional service, and build a thriving community for our customers. If you’re passionate about customer success and ready to own the moment, we’d love to hear from you!

 

About DataSnipper

Audit and finance are still massively manual and we are changing that. DataSnipper is a $1B, bootstrapped unicorn with 600,000+ users across 180+ countries, already embedded in the daily workflows of top audit and accounting firms.

Now, we are taking things further with our Excel Agent, bringing AI directly into where the work actually happens. Unlike generic AI tools, we do not sit on the sidelines. Our AI operates inside Excel, with access to real documents and audit evidence, meaning it does not just generate answers, it does the work, with full traceability.

We are not just applying AI, we are redefining how audit gets done. If you want to build something category-defining at scale, this is the place.

 

What You Will Do

  • Act as a Trusted Advisor: Serve as a strategic partner to key stakeholders including Audit Partners and Managers, Controllers, Finance Directors, and IT decision-makers, guiding them through business transformation enabled by DataSnipper.

  • Drive Business Transformation: Help customers reimagine their workflows and processes, demonstrating how DataSnipper’s AI-powered capabilities can deliver measurable efficiency gains, cost savings, and quality improvements across audit and finance functions.

  • Deliver Strategic Consultative Solutions: Provide expert guidance tailored to each customer’s unique business challenges, helping them optimise audit and finance workflows and achieve their strategic objectives using DataSnipper.

  • Champion Product Adoption and Value Realisation: Conduct comprehensive training sessions, establish regular Business Reviews, and develop success plans that ensure customers adopt DataSnipper features and realise maximum business value.

  • Build Deep Customer Relationships: Cultivate strong, long-term partnerships built on trust, deep industry understanding, and a genuine commitment to your customers’ success and business outcomes.

  • Collaborate Cross-Functionally: Partner with Product, Engineering, Sales, and Solutions Engineering teams, sharing customer insights on workflow challenges, use cases, and technical requirements to drive product innovation.

  • Advocate for Customer Success: Deeply understand your customers’ audit methodologies, compliance requirements, and business goals, providing feedback internally to ensure DataSnipper addresses real-world needs.

  • Support Strategic Growth: Identify and drive expansion opportunities within your portfolio, working with Sales to demonstrate ROI, facilitate pilots, and expand adoption across teams and service lines.

  • Ensure Seamless Technical Implementation & Platform Expertise: Partner with customers on onboarding, including setup, AI configuration, and workflow customisation, while staying current on DataSnipper’s platform, AI capabilities, and automation best practices.

  • Lead Strategic Engagements: Plan and facilitate in-person and virtual sessions with audit and finance teams to drive adoption, share transformation best practices, and address challenges that could impact retention.

  • Develop Comprehensive Success Plans: Create strategic roadmaps for each customer, outlining transformation goals, adoption milestones, expansion opportunities, engagement tactics, and success metrics.

  • Monitor Health and Business Impact: Track and forecast key metrics including user engagement, feature utilisation, business value delivered, expansion opportunities, retention risks, and technical health indicators.

     

What You Bring

  • Trusted Advisor Mindset: Passion for being a strategic partner to customers, building deep trust-based relationships, and driving business transformation that delivers exceptional value.

  • Business Transformation Focus: Proven ability to help customers reimagine processes and workflows, demonstrating how technology can drive measurable business outcomes.

  • Accountability and Ownership: Strong sense of ownership and the drive to master your craft, take initiative, and ensure no detail is overlooked.

  • Collaborative Spirit: Thrives in cross-functional teamwork and builds meaningful partnerships with customers and internal stakeholders.

  • Adaptability and Growth Mindset: Learns quickly and thrives in a dynamic, fast-paced environment where customer needs and priorities evolve.

  • Excellence in Communication: Professional fluency in English and Dutch or French (written and spoken), with the ability to engage stakeholders at all levels - from audit associates to C-suite.
